body: Approach (from interviews and fund behaviour): (1) Stay anchored to normalised earnings and valuations; refuse to pay bubble multiples (tech 1999-2000, realty 2007, quality-consumer at extreme P/Es). (2) Accept underperformance during bubbles - 'when you avoid certain bubbles, the returns take a hit.' (3) Overweight unloved large caps when they trade well below history, typically financials, energy, power and capital goods, and hold for multi-year mean reversion. (4) Low turnover, long horizon. Results: ~20% CAGR over ~20 years vs ~10% for the Nifty, with painful stretches (2013, 2015, 2018-20). Lesson from the PSU-heavy phase: cheapness without a catalyst (earnings upgrade, capex cycle, bad-loan clean-up) can last years and cause investor redemptions; for an individual, size contrarian large-cap bets so you can wait, and define the catalyst you're waiting for.
title: Prashant Jain: large-cap valuation discipline through bubbles

body: Rule as tested (2026-11-20 backtest, signals 2021-2024). Trigger: Form 4 code P purchases of common stock by >=2 distinct directors or officers with trade dates within 30 days; exclude 10b5-1 trades (checkbox or footnote), 10%-owner-only filers, option exercises/grants, price < $1, preferred/warrants/units. Signal date = filing date of the second insider's Form 4 (no look-ahead); enter at next trading-day close; one signal per issuer per 365 days. Universe: market cap $300M-$10B, ex SPACs/funds, listed >= 180 days; biotech/pharma handled separately (binary events). Hold 6 or 12 months; compare with 5 random same-size firms on the same date and with IWM. Result: no reliable excess return vs matched controls (12m mean 0.0%, CI -4.8% to +5.0%, hit 44.9%; see insight:bt-us-insider-clusters-2021-2024). Status: REJECTED as a standalone strategy for 2021-2024; keep only as a research-queue trigger. Untested refinements worth a pre-registered out-of-sample test: Cohen-Malloy-Pomorski opportunistic-only buyers (no same-month trade in prior 3 years), buy size >= 10% of the insider's existing stake, sub-$1B or bank issuers, poorly covered names; analogous test on India SEBI PIT Reg 7 disclosures.
